# Room Booking Rules
Quillbrook Village Hall is a fictional organisation.

## 1. General conditions
1.1 These rules were adopted on 12 February 2025.
1.2 Rooms may be hired by adults aged 18 or over.
1.3 The named hirer is responsible for the entire booking.
1.4 The hirer must give a contact address and telephone number.

## 2. Booking requests
2.1 Requests may be submitted up to 12 months in advance.
2.2 Requests must arrive at least three calendar days before the event.
2.3 The booking officer checks availability before accepting a request.
2.4 A booking is accepted only when written acceptance is issued.
2.5 Payment deadlines are set out in hall-fees.md section 6.
2.6 Failure to pay the booking deposit cancels an accepted booking.

## 3. Opening hours
3.1 Monday to Thursday: 08:00 to 22:00.
3.2 Friday and Saturday: 08:00 to 23:00.
3.3 Sunday: 09:00 to 21:00.
3.4 All guests must leave by the relevant closing time.
3.5 Setup and clearing must take place within booked hours.

## 4. Room capacities
4.1 Main Hall: maximum 90 people.
4.2 Meeting Room: maximum 24 people.
4.3 Combined events may not exceed 100 people in the building.
4.4 Capacities include organisers, performers and children.
4.5 Fire safety requirements in hall-safety.md also apply.

## 5. Access and equipment
5.1 Keys are collected from the booking officer by arrangement.
5.2 Keys may not be copied or passed to another hirer.
5.3 Equipment must be requested when the booking is made.
5.4 Equipment charges follow hall-fees.md section 4.
5.5 Hirers must report missing or faulty equipment before use.

## 6. Changes
6.1 Changes to dates or rooms require written approval.
6.2 A date change counts as cancellation and a new booking.
6.3 Cancellation charges are governed by hall-refunds.md.

# Booking Desk Quick Guide
Quillbrook Village Hall is a fictional organisation.

## 1. Using this guide
This sheet was last refreshed on 10 July 2026.
It is a convenience summary, not a governing document.
The governing documents and hall-changes.md always prevail.
Check the event and cancellation dates before quoting a price.

## 2. Rooms and prices
The Main Hall normally costs £28 an hour.
The Meeting Room costs £12 an hour.
The kitchen costs another £8 per booking.
Bookings normally last at least two hours per room.
Registered village groups generally get 25% off room hire.
Projectors cost £15 and portable speakers cost £10.
Display boards cost £5 per set.
Equipment and kitchen charges do not receive the group discount.

## 3. Booking and payment
Bookings can be requested up to a year ahead.
Allow at least three days before the event.
A booking is not accepted until confirmed in writing.
A £30 booking deposit is normally required.
The outstanding hire bill is generally due two weeks before the event.
Alcohol events also need a £100 damage deposit.

## 4. Opening and attendance
Monday to Thursday events now finish by 21:30.
Friday and Saturday events may run until 23:00.
Sunday events finish by 21:00.
The Main Hall holds up to 90 people.
The Meeting Room holds up to 24 people.
Combined events are limited to 100 people in the building.

## 5. Music and cancellations
Friday and Saturday amplified music stops at 21:30.
Music stops by 21:00 on other days.
Early cancellation may qualify for a full or partial refund.
Mid-range cancellations now generally receive 25% rather than 50%.
The booking deposit is normally kept when a hirer cancels.

## 6. Questions to refer
Check hall-refunds.md before promising any repayment.
Refer safety issues immediately to a trustee.
Do not settle disputed damage charges at the booking desk.

**Everything was due on 2 October 2025, the day your booking was accepted.**

- The event was 10 days after acceptance (2 to 12 October 2025). That is fewer than 14 days ahead.
- hall-fees.md 6.3 says bookings made fewer than 14 days ahead require full payment at acceptance. That covers the whole hire charge, including the £30 booking deposit.
- The usual deadlines don't apply to you. The deposit would normally be due within seven days of acceptance (6.1), which would have been 9 October. The balance would normally be due 14 days before the event (6.2), which would have been 28 September, before your booking existed.
- If you served alcohol, the separate £100 damage deposit (5.2–5.3) would also have been payable. The rules don't give it its own deadline, so I'd assume it fell due at acceptance too.
- Under hall-bookings.md 2.6, failing to pay the booking deposit cancels an accepted booking.

Nothing in the committee changes register (hall-changes.md) alters these payment rules. The dates are in the past relative to today (15 October 2026), so this assumes your question is about the 2025 event.
